title: Bilateral Common Carotid Artery Stenosis in Mice: A Model of Chronic Cerebral Hypoperfusion-Induced Vascular Cognitive Impairment
author: Masashi Kakae
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Materials and reagents Mice: Male C57BL/6J, 8–12 weeks old, 20–30 g Isoflurane (Viatris, catalog number: 901036504)

steps.title: Gather mice and reagents
steps.instruction: Use male C57BL/6J mice, 8–12 weeks old, weighing 20–30 g, and isoflurane (Viatris, catalog number 901036504).

steps.title: Induce and maintain anesthesia
steps.instruction: Place the mouse in an incubation box and anesthetize with 3 % isoflurane in 30 % O₂ / 70 % N₂O for approximately 3 min; then maintain anesthesia throughout the surgery with 1.5 % isoflurane in the same gas mixture delivered via a face mask.

steps.title: Expose and isolate common carotid arteries
steps.instruction: Position the anesthetized mouse supine with limbs spread, make a 1–1.5 cm ventral cervical midline skin incision, separate the submandibular glands laterally to expose the trachea, move the sternocleidomastoid muscle laterally using a handmade wire hook with a weight to reveal the CCA sheath, and carefully isolate each common carotid artery (CCA) from surrounding tissue and the vagus nerve with forceps, avoiding any damage.

steps.title: Place microcoils to create stenosis
steps.instruction: For each CCA, gently lift the isolated artery, position a microcoil vertically beneath it so the artery is centered, twine the CCA around one side of the coil, then twine it around the opposite side to complete the stenosis, remove the wire hook, and replace the sternocleidomastoid muscle and submandibular glands; repeat the procedure on the contralateral CCA.

steps.title: Close incision and post‑operative care
steps.instruction: Suture the cervical skin incision with three interrupted 5‑0 silk sutures, return the mouse to a clean cage, and house at a constant ambient temperature of 22 ± 2 °C under a 12 h light/12 h dark cycle with food and water available ad libitum.

steps.title: Sham operation (no microcoil)
steps.instruction: Perform the anesthesia, exposure, and isolation steps exactly as above, but omit the microcoil placement; replace the muscles as described, then suture and house the mouse using the same procedures as in the completion step.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol or parts of it has been used and validated in the following research articles: Shibata et al. [10]. White Matter Lesions and Glial Activation in a Novel Mouse Model of Chronic Cerebral Hypoperfusion. Stroke (Figures 1A–C, 2B, and Table 1). Miyanohara et al. [11]. TRPM2 Channel Aggravates CNS Inflammation and Cognitive Impairment via Activation of Microglia in Chronic Cerebral Hypoperfusion. J Neurosci (Figures 1F and 2A, B, D, E). Kakae et al. [12]. The astrocytic TRPA1 channel mediates an intrinsic protective response to vascular cognitive impairment via LIF production. Sci Adv (Figure 1P–R and supplementary figure 1D).
